description:
NASA will release the first images from its Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope during a live stream from the American Geophysical Union (AGU) Annual Meeting in San Francisco.

The images will showcase the unique scientific capabilities of Roman, which will soon capture deep, panoramic, never-before-seen views of the universe to explore the mysteries of dark energy, dark matter, and worlds outside our solar system.

vid_urls.title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Undocking
vid_urls.description:
Watch as a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft undocks from the International Space Station and begins its journey back to Earth. The uncrewed Dragon is carrying scientific research samples and hardware including a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct and frozen microbial samples.

The spacecraft will reenter Earth's atmosphere Nov. 21 and will splash down off the Californian coast at approximately 5:04 p.m. EST (2:04 p.m. PST, 2204 UTC).

Learn more about NASA's SpaceX CRS-35 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crs-35/
Get daily updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/

description:
Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft.

NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California will host a moderated discussion with mission members and NASA leadership about the status of Voyager 1 and 2, the unique science the twin probes continue to gather in interstellar space, and the challenges of keeping the spacecraft operating for so long over such vast distances. A Q&A with media and other audience members will follow. In addition, there also will be a preview of the upcoming NASA+ Voyager documentary, planned for release in 2027 for the mission’s 50th anniversary.

The participants will be:
- Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, Washington
- Jonathan Lunine, chief scientist, NASA JPL, and professor of planetary science, Caltech
- Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager, NASA JPL
- Linda Spilker, Voyager project scientist, NASA JPL
- Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager, NASA JPL
- Jamie Rankin, Voyager deputy project scientist, Princeton University
location: Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Pasadena, CA, USA

name: RS-25 Engine Test

vid_urls.title: NASA Stennis Live Stream
vid_urls.description:
NASA tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Nov. 18, 2026, on the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi.

Test teams fired the developmental engine for three minutes and 20 seconds (200 seconds).

While this developmental engine will not be used in flight, the hot fire test provides NASA and NASA’s prime contractor L3Harris Technologies with the capability to capture critical data to improve engine performance and reliability for future Artemis missions.

description: NASA is conducting a hot fire of an RS-25 engine as part of certification testing for future SLS (Space Launch System) rockets.
location: Fred Haise Test Stand, NASA’s Stennis Space Center
